         Subject(s):     Escape room; Escape room establishment; Puzzle room; Use group, escape or puzzle room; Use
                         group, amusements; Zoning Use Group classification (UG), Use Group 8A, Amusement; UG 12;
                         Special Amusement Buildings


I.     Background
       An “escape room,” also known as “puzzle room,” is a new type of business establishment that provides indoor
       amusement in which occupants are encouraged to solve a challenge in order to escape from a room or series
       of rooms. The doors inside such establishments may be locked or obscured as a part of the amusement
       experience. Escape room establishments and similar operations are considered “special amusement
       buildings” under the building code and are required to comply with applicable zoning and building code
       requirements.


II.    Classification of Zoning Use Group.
       Zoning Resolution (ZR) section 32-17 states in part,
       “Use Group 8 consists primarily of amusement or service establishments which:
       (1) are appropriate in local service districts to serve nearby residential areas; or
       (2) depend on a wide service radius and may appropriately be located in secondary or major
           commercial centers.

       Since these establishments are generally patronized by customers for special purposes not
       associated with retail shopping, they are appropriate neither in local shopping areas nor in the
       restricted central commercial areas.”



       ZR Section 32-21 states in part,

       “Use Group 12 consists primarily of fairly large entertainment facilities that:
        (1) have a wide service area and generate considerable pedestrian, automotive or truck traffic; and
        (2) are, therefore, appropriate only in secondary, major or central commercial areas.

        Certain public service establishments are also included.”
        Escape room establishments are typically provided as amusement establishments in local commercial or
        manufacturing districts serving nearby residential or commercial areas, with patronage similar to billiard
        parlors, pool halls and theatres. Therefore, they may be classified under zoning UG 8A “Amusement” or UG
        12A “Amusement.” Escape room establishments are permitted as-of-right in the zoning districts where UG 8A
        or 12A are permitted as-of-right.


III.    Building Code Occupancy Classification.
        2014 Building Code (BC) section 411.2 definition states in part,

        “SPECIAL AMUSEMENT BUILDING. A special amusement building is any temporary or permanent
        building or portion thereof that is occupied for amusement, entertainment or educational purposes
        and that contains a device or system that conveys passengers or provides a walkway along, around
        or over a course in any direction so arranged that the means of egress path is not readily apparent
        due to visual or audio distractions or is intentionally confounded or is not readily available because of
        the nature of the attraction or mode of conveyance through the building or structure.”

        Escape room establishments are typically arranged so that the means of egress path is intentionally
        confounded and not readily available for the entertainment or amusement of the occupants. Therefore, escape
        room establishments in buildings or portions thereof shall be classified as either Occupancy Group B or A-3
        under the 2014 Building Code and shall comply with the applicable provisions for such Occupancy
        Classification. Where specifically requested and permitted, work performed in prior code buildings may
        comply with the 1968 Code (subject to the exceptions in AC 28-101.4.3), and escape room establishments
        located in prior code buildings may be designed in accordance with the requirements for Occupancy Group F-
        3.

        Occupant loads and classifications shall be determined as outlined below:
           Pursuant to BC 1004.1.3 and AC 27-358(a), the occupant load shall be calculated as 15 net s.f./occupant.
           If the calculated occupant load is less than 75 persons, pursuant to BC 303.1 exception 2, such
            establishment shall be classified as Group B Occupancy.
           If the calculated occupant load is 75 persons or more, pursuant to BC 303.1, such establishment shall be
            classified as Group A-3 Occupancy.
           For escape room establishments in prior code buildings, such establishments may be designed in
            accordance with the requirements for Occupancy Group F-3, including place of assembly pursuant to 27-
            257. Such escape room establishments shall be designated with the equivalent Occupancy Classification
            from the 2014 Code for the purposes of filing job applications and obtaining a Certificate of Occupancy.


IV.     Administrative Requirements.
        AC 28-118.3.1 states,
        “§28-118.3.1 Change of occupancy or use. No building, open lot or portion thereof hereafter
        altered so as to change from one occupancy group to another, or from one zoning use group to
        another, either in whole or in part, shall be occupied or used unless and until the commissioner has
        issued a certificate of occupancy certifying that the alteration work for which the permit was issued
        has been completed substantially in accordance with the approved construction documents and the
        provisions of this code and other applicable laws and rules for the new occupancy or use.”
        AC 28-118.3.2 states,
        “§28-118.3.2 Changes inconsistent with existing certificate of occupancy. No change shall be
        made to a building, open lot or portion thereof inconsistent with the last issued certificate of
        occupancy or, where applicable, inconsistent with the last issued certificate of completion for such

      The creation of an escape room establishment in an existing building shall require a new or amended
      certificate of occupancy and must demonstrate compliance with the applicable code requirements and the
      requirements of this bulletin. Such job application shall be filed as Alteration Type I and identified in PW1A as

      zoning use group (UG) 8A or 12A, the applicable building code occupancy classification (A-3 or B) , and the
      description as “Escape Room Establishment per BB 2019-008.”

      If the calculated occupant load is 75 persons or more, a Certificate of Operation shall be required for a place of
      assembly in accordance with BC 303.2.


V.    Egress and Fire Protection Requirements.
      If the job application is to be reviewed under the 2014 Code, the following requirements shall be applicable:
         If the calculated occupant load is less than 75 persons, egress shall comply with provisions required for
          occupancy group B in Chapter 10.
         If the calculated occupant load is 75 persons or more, egress shall comply with provisions required for
          occupancy group A-3 in Chapter 10.
         Fire protection shall comply with provisions in Chapter 9 as required for the applicable occupancy, group B
          or group A-3.

      If the job application is requested and permitted to be reviewed under the prior code, the following
      requirements shall be applicable:
         If the calculated occupant load is less than 75 persons, egress shall comply with provisions required for
          occupancy F-3 in AC Subchapter 6.
         If the calculated occupant load is 75 persons or more, egress shall comply with provisions required for
          occupancy group F-3 in AC Subchapter 6 and 8.
         Fire protection shall comply with provisions in Chapter 9 of the 2014 Building Code as required for the
          applicable occupancy group, group B (less 75 persons) or group A-3 (75 or more persons).


VI.   Additional Code Requirements.
      Regardless of the occupant load or allowance to use a prior code, provisions in BC 411 governing special
      amusement buildings shall apply to all escape room establishments. All of the following additional
      requirements shall be applicable:

      A. Fire alarm control unit location. The fire alarm control unit shall be located within the designated
         surveillance room or area, unless the escape room establishments are protected by a building’s fire alarm
         system with voice communication capabilities.

      B. Use of pre-recorded messages prohibited. Use of pre-recorded messages, as set forth in BC
         907.2.12.2(4), is not allowed.

      C. Fire alarm system monitoring. Fire alarm system shall be monitored by an approved central station in
         accordance with BC 907.6.5.

      D. Mechanical ventilation. Mechanical ventilation shall be provided in accordance with Mechanical Code
         Chapter 4, and windows shall not be credited as means of natural ventilation.

      E. Exit requirements. Exits from all rooms, spaces or series of spaces within the establishments shall be
         open and readily available upon activation by automatic fire alarm system, automatic sprinkler system, or
         a manual control at a constantly attended location. Doors used as part of the means of egress serving
         such rooms, spaces or series of spaces occupied by persons whose movements are controlled may be

           locked when equipped with egress control devices which shall unlock both manually and by at least one of
           the following means:
           1. Activation of a smoke detection system installed in accordance with BC 907.2.12;
           2. Activation of an automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with BC 903.3.1.1;
           3. Activation of an approved manual fire alarm system pull station;
           4. A signal from a manual release located in the designated surveillance room or area; or
           5. A signal from a listed hardware that incorporates a built-in switch and is installed in accordance with
              BC 1008.1.9.8.

       F. Exit marking requirement. When photoluminescent signs are installed, activating light source and
          viewing distance shall be in accordance with the listing and markings of such signs.


VII.   Additional Fire Department Requirements.

       A. Surveillance. When the facility is in operation, all escape room establishments shall be under continuous
          surveillance from a designated room or area located in the same facility. Such surveillance shall be
          conducted either through a window or an approved type of closed-circuit monitoring system.

       B. Staffing. The surveillance shall be conducted by a person holding a Fire Department Certificate of Fitness
          for Supervision of Special Amusements (F-63). Operation of one-way emergency voice communication
          system shall be performed by a person holding a Fire Department Certificate of Fitness (F-53). The
          Commissioner or the Fire Commissioner may require additional staff if the facility presents heightened
          safety concerns.

       C. Decorations and scenery. Decorations and scenery shall be flame-resistant in accordance with the New
          York City Fire Code requirements.
